meta_description: Event-log truth exposes the rework loops that every automation program quietly funds.

blocks.x: Event-log truth exposes the rework loops that every automation program quietly funds.

Process mining is the cheapest AI you will buy is not a slogan; it is a delivery position. The evidence is consistent across industries — the constraint is rarely technology; it is whether the operating model takes this seriously from sprint one.

items: Variant analysis routinely finds 10-30 rework loops per major process.
Task mining quantifies swivel-chair waste that surveys miss.
Conformance monitoring keeps target-state design honest after go-live.

blocks.x: Three questions to ask your current vendors

items: What is the classical baseline every proposed capability must beat, measured on identical data?
Who signs the go/no-go gate, and what evidence do they require before signing?
Show us a negative result you documented: the discipline is the product.

blocks.x: Programs stall when the operating model is treated as an afterthought — the technology works in week six and the organization has not changed in week sixty, so the capability Silently degrades into shelfware.

items: Pre-agreed criteria and locked baselines before build; the demo is the least important artifact.
Named owners, run models and escalation paths agreed with the operating team, not for it.
Replay trails, control tests and documentation as artifacts of the build — never reconstructed.

blocks.x: Evidence-backed portfolios typically double the accuracy of workshop-estimated business cases.
